continues.

Grande Counties...

and flood-prone locations is occurring.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 24 at 2:48PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
At 247 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 14
miles northwest of Dulce, moving northeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation and
outdoor objects is possible.

Locations impacted include...
Pagosa Springs, Chimney Rock, Juanita, Pagosa Junction, Gato, and
Lonetree.

This includes the following highways...
U.S. Highway 84 in Colorado between mile markers 17 and 27.
U.S. Highway 160 in Colorado between mile markers 130 and 146.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Mayaguez and Vicinity; Culebra
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 24 at 4:48PM AST until October 26 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...Beaches along the northwest to northeast beaches of
Puerto Rico and Culebra.

* WHEN...Through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Colorado...

San Juan River at Pagosa Springs affecting Archuleta County.

* WHAT...The San Juan River is still running high but expected to
remain above bankfull through midnight tonight. Additional rainfall
could cause the river to rise, but it is expected to continue
decreasing through Sunday.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Pagosa Springs.

* WHEN...Until Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 10.3 feet, Water is flowing over the yards of homes in
the San Juan River Village northeast of Pagosa Springs.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:00 PM MDT Saturday the stage was 9.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is currently below minor flood stage but is
expected to remain above bankfull through midnight tonight. It is
expected to continue falling to 9.0 feet Sunday morning and 7.3
feet Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/gjt.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 600 AM MDT.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 1:34PM PDT until October 29 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.9ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Francisco Bay, Monterey
Bay and Big Sur Coast.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 11:07 AM
Sunday 10/25, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 11:39 AM
Monday 10/26, 1.8 ft above normal (7.6 ft MLLW) at 12:15 PM
Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 12:56 PM
Wednesday 10/28, and 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 01:43
PM Thursday 10/29. These predictions include up to 1.0 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 24 at 12:16PM AKDT until October 27 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 2 to 4 feet above the normal
high tide line. For the Coastal Flood Watch, potential for
another round of more significant elevated waters around Monday
night. Water Levels between 3 and 5 feet are possible.

* WHERE...Kivalina and Red Dog Dock.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM AKDT Tuesday.
For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Monday night through
late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur with the High Surf
advisory. For the Coastal Flood Watch, minor coastal flooding
is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...South to southwest winds will continue to
gust up to 40 mph through the weekend. Strong winds continue
into early next week.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Precautions should be taken to protect property.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 12:16PM AKDT until October 25 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. Water levels will rise 4 to 6 feet above the normal
high tide line along the Bering Strait Coast, including Teller
and Brevig Mission. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 2 to 4 ft.

* WHERE...Bering Strait Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 PM AKDT
Sunday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 10 PM Sunday to 4 AM
AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Water levels 4 to 6 feet above the normal high tide
line in Wales may cause water to overflow from Village Creek
into low lying areas behind town. For Teller and Brevig
Mission, minor flooding in low lying areas. Water levels will
gradually drop through the weekend. Localized beach erosion
may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...South to southwest winds will continue to
gust up to 40 mph through the weekend. Strong winds continue
into early next week.
